title: When You Can't Stop Overthinking at Night
music_prompt:
A slow, quiet, emotional lo-fi ballad for late-night overthinking. Soft duet: a gentle, breathy female voice and a warm, low, calm male voice, singing softly and close to the microphone, never loud. Soft felt piano, warm analog pads, light vinyl crackle, steady gentle rain in the background, a very soft muted lo-fi beat at 70 BPM, a little sub bass. Key of D major with melancholic minor chords. Most of the track is instrumental with soft wordless humming; only the short verses and chorus below are sung. No build-up, no loud chorus, no belting, no sudden changes, no fade-in or fade-out: it starts and ends at the same soft level so it loops seamlessly. Feeling: lonely but safe, like someone quietly understands you.

Lyrics:
[Intro: soft humming, female and male]

[Verse 1, female]
The city's asleep, but my thoughts are awake,
counting the words I was too scared to say.

[Verse 1, male]
Rain on the window, slow and so kind,
telling me softly to rest my mind.

[Chorus, both, very soft]
It's okay, it's okay, let the night be slow,
some things you carry, you can let go.

[Instrumental: piano and rain, soft humming]

[Outro, both, whispered]
Let it go, let the night be slow.
